subject.identity: Server.ListenAddr default vs the documented :8081 / --port contract

title: Every document tells you to run `./slabledger` and reach :8081; the bare binary binds 127.0.0.1:8080, and `server --port N` is a no-op without --web

evidence.claim: The listen address defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080 and is only re-derived from Mode.WebPort inside FromFlags, and only when Mode.WebMode is true. WebMode has no default and no env binding — it is set exclusively by the -web/--web flag.
evidence.command: git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:internal/platform/config/defaults.go | sed -n '7,16p' ; git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:internal/platform/config/loader.go | sed -n '231,259p'

evidence.claim: cmd/slabledger/server.go only falls back to WebPort when ListenAddr is the empty string. It is never empty — the default is a non-empty literal — so Mode.WebPort never reaches the listener except through the WebMode branch above.
HTTP_LISTEN_ADDR cannot rescue the bare invocation: .env.example ships it empty, and envString skips empty values.

Four places document the bare invocation and promise :8081 — including the binary's own help text, which additionally advertises `slabledger server --port 9090` as the way to change the port. Without --web that flag parses and is then discarded.
evidence.command: git grep -n './slabledger$\|Start web server on :8081\|localhost:8081\|go run ./cmd/slabledger' 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6 -- CLAUDE.md README.md docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ; git show 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6:cmd/slabledger/main.go | grep -n 'default port 8081\|--port 9090'

README.md:20-22: ./slabledger  /  # Open http://localhost:8081
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:256:| Frontend proxy 502 | Backend not running on :8081. Start backend: `go run ./cmd/slabledger` |

evidence.claim: Every invocation that actually works passes --web explicitly, which is why the drift has stayed invisible: the Makefile run target and the Docker CMD both do. Nothing in the repo runs the binary the way the documentation says to.

The consequence is not cosmetic. The Vite dev proxy hard-codes localhost:8081, and the devcontainer publishes 8081, so a developer following README.md gets a server on a port nothing proxies to — bound to 127.0.0.1, which is additionally unreachable through the devcontainer's published port.
